finding.title: Trim or split the 8 test/sync files exceeding the 400-line AG-3 cap

evidence.quote: /// T5.lifecycle regression tests — mirror wipe on revoke/resign/sign-out.
/// Acceptance test for Plan §F Phase 4 deliverable 2.
/// Per-curriculum completion doc-ID and tombstone-propagation tests.
/// Wave 2 — S7: the SyncOrchestrator singleton invariant.

finding.why: wc -l over the batch shows 8 of 16 files exceed the 400-line hand-written-file cap: tutored_mirror_wipe_test.dart (858), sync_status_emission_test.dart (672), sync_rework_curriculum_completion_doc_id_test.dart (662), sync_rework_orchestrator_test.dart (642), sync_orchestrator_drain_triggers_test.dart (514), sync_rework_push_test.dart (455), study_day_config_sync_test.dart (409), sync_rework_profile_programs_pull_test.dart (405). For 3 of these the direct cause is the duplicated-fake pattern (see companion finding); the rest are large multi-scenario suites that would read and diff more easily split along their own top-level group() boundaries.
finding.recommendation: Apply the shared-fake fix first for the 3 fake-driven files; for the rest, split by the file's own group() boundaries (e.g. one file per T/S/P trigger in tutored_mirror_wipe_test.dart).
acceptance_criteria: `find learning_tracker/test/sync -name '*_test.dart' | xargs wc -l | awk '$1>400'` returns empty or only an explicit recorded ratchet baseline

finding.title: Use FakeLocalDayClock instead of wall-clock (SystemLocalDayClock/DateTime.now()) in test/sync hermetic tests
finding.rule: TQ-6 (pending: extend hermetic-test check to test/)
finding.why: stage_definition_single_path_test.dart wires the real system clock into OutboxSyncWriteFacade under test; its sibling study_day_config_sync_test.dart uses FakeLocalDayClock(DateTime.utc(...)) for the identical facade, showing the fixed-clock convention exists and was simply not followed here. tutored_listener_supervisor_test.dart uses DateTime.now() three times (lines 191, 313, 354) for filler payload values. Neither instance drives a flaky assertion today, but both stand as standing violations of the hermetic-test rule the moment a future edit asserts against the timestamp, and both make the test's inputs non-reproducible from a bug report.
finding.recommendation: Replace `const SystemLocalDayClock()` with `FakeLocalDayClock(DateTime.utc(...))` in stage_definition_single_path_test.dart; replace the three DateTime.now() payload fillers in tutored_listener_supervisor_test.dart with a fixed ISO string.
acceptance_criteria: grep for 'SystemLocalDayClock' and 'DateTime.now()' in stage_definition_single_path_test.dart and tutored_listener_supervisor_test.dart returns empty

finding.title: Route two_device_sync_test.dart's S1/S3 through the real MergeRouter instead of hand-decoding outbox JSON

evidence.quote: final data = jsonDecode(row.payload) as Map<String, dynamic>;

finding.why: test/sync/two_device_sync_test.dart and test/integration/two_device_sync_test.dart share the exact same name and the same group label ('I-5: two-device sync scenarios' / 'Two-device convergence test harness (I-5)'), created about an hour apart on the same day. The integration version carries @Tags(['i5','two_device_sync']) and drives the real MergeRouter/CompletionEventMerger/EntityMerger stack — it is the file docs/sync-conflict-resolution.md names as the canonical I-5 harness (completion set-union, track-deactivation LWW, idempotent re-merge). The file in this batch has no tags at all and, for S1 ('completion propagates to Device B'), never imports MergeRouter/EntityMerger — it hand-decodes the outbox JSON payload and calls completionEventDao.appendEvent directly, bypassing every line of the actual merge/dispatch code Device B's real pull uses. A regression in CompletionEventMerger's field mapping or LWW comparison would not be caught here; a reader trusting the group name would believe cross-device merge logic is under test when it isn't, and it also doesn't cover track-deactivation LWW at all (only the integration twin does).
finding.recommendation: Either delete test/sync/two_device_sync_test.dart's S1/S3 in favor of the tag-carrying, merge-router-driven test/integration/two_device_sync_test.dart (keeping S2's soft-delete-outbox scenario, relocated since it's not duplicated there), or rewrite S1's simulated pull to dispatch through the real MergeRouter/CompletionEventMerger so the test exercises production code and add the i5/two_device_sync tags for consistency.
acceptance_criteria: Only one file covers I-5 two-device completion propagation end-to-end through MergeRouter/CompletionEventMerger, or the two files are clearly differentiated in name and purpose.
Any surviving two_device_sync_test.dart file carries @Tags(['i5','two_device_sync']) matching its sibling.

finding.title: Add a test for OutboxSyncWriteFacade's onEnqueueDrain chain — write_tee_status_update_test.dart only unit-tests recordDrainAttempt() in isolation
finding.why: The file's own docstring names the bug precisely: OutboxSyncWriteFacade.onEnqueueDrain called drain() without the follow-up recordDrainAttempt(), so the sync badge stayed falsely 'Synced'. The fix — chaining recordDrainAttempt() after drain() — is correctly wired today at sync_providers.dart:105-108 (verified by reading it). But both tests in this file build a bare SyncOrchestratorImpl and call `orchestrator.recordDrainAttempt()` directly; neither constructs an OutboxSyncWriteFacade or exercises the onEnqueueDrain closure at all. recordDrainAttempt() is a one-line wrapper (`=> _recomputeOutboxStatus()`), so this mostly re-tests status computation, not the chaining bug. There is no test file for sync_providers.dart or outbox_sync_write_facade.dart anywhere in test/ (checked via `find`), so nothing would fail if a future provider refactor drops the recordDrainAttempt() call again — the exact original bug could silently reappear with this whole suite green.
finding.recommendation: Add a test (e.g. test/features/sync/presentation/providers/sync_providers_test.dart or test/features/sync/data/outbox_sync_write_facade_test.dart, mirroring AG-5) that builds the real OutboxSyncWriteFacade/onEnqueueDrain closure with a failing pipeline and asserts the sync-status badge updates without a manual recordDrainAttempt() call from the test body.
acceptance_criteria: A test exists at a path mirroring lib/features/sync/presentation/providers/sync_providers.dart or lib/features/sync/data/outbox_sync_write_facade.dart.
That test drives OutboxSyncWriteFacade's write-tee (enqueue → onEnqueueDrain) end to end and asserts recordDrainAttempt() fires without the test calling it directly.
